title: Allocating Transaction Price
description: Allocate consideration among performance obligations using relative standalone selling prices.
html:
Step 4 — Allocate the transaction price

When a contract contains more than one performance obligation, the transaction price generally must be allocated among those obligations.

Allocation is generally based on the relative standalone selling prices of the promised goods or services.

Standalone selling price

The standalone selling price is the price at which a company would sell a promised good or service separately to a customer.

Example

A company sells a package containing:

Product standalone price $800
Service standalone price $200
Total standalone prices $1,000

The customer pays a bundled contract price of $900.

Step 1 — Determine relative percentages

Product: $800 ÷ $1,000 = 80%
Service: $200 ÷ $1,000 = 20%

Step 2 — Allocate the $900 transaction price

Product: $900 × 80% = $720
Service: $900 × 20% = $180
Allocated to Product $720
Allocated to Service $180
Total Transaction Price $900

Always check

The amounts allocated to all performance obligations should add back to the transaction price.

$720 + $180 = $900 ✓

General formula

Allocation = Transaction Price × (Standalone Price of Obligation ÷ Total Standalone Selling Prices)

quiz.prompt: A contract contains Product A with a standalone selling price of $600 and Service B with a standalone selling price of $400. The bundled transaction price is $800. How much is allocated to Product A?
quiz.explanation: Product A represents $600 ÷ $1,000 = 60% of total standalone selling prices. $800 × 60% = $480.
